message.content:
**Short answer:** Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta, but it’s usually handled by the **City of Atlanta Police Department** (or the local police agency) rather than the city council itself. The council can take up the issue at a public meeting or through a constituent request, but the actual enforcement is done by the police or the city’s Noise Enforcement Program. --- ## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta | Step | What to Do | Where/How | |------|------------|-----------| | **1. Identify the source** | Determine whether the noise is coming from a residential, commercial, or industrial property. | N/A | | **2. Call 311 (Atlanta Police)** | 311 is the city’s non-emergency hotline for reporting noise violations. | Phone: **(404) 576-3111** (or dial 311 on your cell phone if you’re in Atlanta) | | **3. Use the Online Portal** | You can submit a noise complaint online via the Atlanta Police Department’s website. | Visit the [APD Noise Complaint page](https://www.atlantapolice.org/311) and fill out the form. | | **4. Provide Details** | Be ready to give:
• Exact address or location of the noise source
• Time and duration of the noise
• Description of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs)
• Your contact information (optional but helpful) | In the phone call or online form | | **5. Follow Up** | After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. If the noise continues, you can call back with the reference number to check status. | Phone or online portal | ### Additional Tips - **Noise Ordinance Hours**: Atlanta’s noise ordinance typically prohibits excessive noise between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m. on weekdays and 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. on weekends. Knowing this helps you determine if the noise violates the ordinance. - **Document Evidence**: If possible, record the noise (audio or video) or keep a log of dates/times. This can help the police assess the complaint. - **Contact Your Council Member**: If you feel the issue isn’t being addressed, you can reach out to your local city council member. They can bring the matter to a council meeting or request a city council hearing. Find your council member here: [Atlanta City Council Members](https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/city-council). --- ## When to Contact the City Council Directly While the police handle enforcement, the city council can: - **Schedule a public hearing** on persistent noise problems in a neighborhood. - **Request a city inspection** of a business or property suspected of violating noise ordinances. - **Advocate for stricter enforcement** or new ordinances if the current ones aren’t effective. If you want the council to intervene, you can: 1. **Call the council office**: Each council member’s office has a phone number listed on the city’s website. 2. **Submit a constituent request**: Many council offices accept written requests via email or an online form. 3. **Attend a council meeting**: Bring your complaint to the agenda and speak during the public comment period. --- ## Quick Reference | Resource | Contact | |----------|---------| | **Atlanta Police 311** | (404) 576-3111 | | **Online Noise Complaint** | https://www.atlantapolice.org/311 | | **City of Atlanta Noise Ordinance** | https://www.atlantaga.gov/sites/default/files/2023-08/Noise%20Ordinance.pdf | | **Council Member Directory** | https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/city-council | --- ### Bottom Line - **File the complaint with the police** (via 311 or online). - **Use the council** if you need a broader policy response or if the police aren’t addressing the issue. - **Keep records** and follow up using the reference number you receive. Feel free to let me know if you need help locating your specific council member or if you’d like more details on the noise ordinance itself!
